text: The model flagged this applicant as high‑risk because two of the key signals point strongly toward a likelihood of default. First, the borrower has two accounts that are 30‑59 days past due; this recent delinquency added the largest boost (+1.16) to the default probability. Second, the revolving‑credit utilization is about 75 % of the available limit, which contributed another sizable increase (+0.89) to the risk score. The only factor that pulled the score down was the debt‑to‑income figure, which is unusually high at 3,114 and gave a modest negative contribution (‑0.34). Overall, the two risk‑raising factors outweigh the small mitigating effect, leading to a 73 % default probability and a “high risk” decision.
